evidence:
Scope and authority: reviewed only quality check 43. Opened the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl: Quality Checks!A44:D44 states "scoring.toml gates zero the reward and skip the scored suite, gates carry no weight, and the functional floor stops a non-working app farming polish/visual." Internal Quality Checks row 44 was read as interpretation, not substituted for the shipped staged profile. Relevant deterministic rows 7, 33 and 36 corroborate the canonical shared scorer, scoring policy, and staged harness. Frozen skill delivery profile and references/quality-checks.md:175-176 require two zero-weight gates plus functional floor. references/staged-task-contract.md:80-109 and references/deterministic-checks.md:40-46 establish the exact policy and ordered execution. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md sections "Gates must exclude convincing dead apps" and "Runtime and model evidence" were applied.

Policy and aggregate mass: all task citations below are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/. tests/scoring.toml:1-11 has [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05. TOML parsing confirmed both gates contain exactly one binary criterion and aggregation="all_pass" (tests/gates/{render,constraints}/judge.toml:14-21). Their local criterion weight 1.0 establishes the binary gate result; it contributes no reward mass because neither gate appears in [weights]. Every scored dimension uses weighted_mean; derived counts and local weight totals are functional 58/32.7, polish 7/4.0, visual 6/6.0. No [judge] block contains a dimension weight. The sum of dimension weights is 1.0, with maximum non-functional mass 0.4.

Scorer behavior was executed locally, read-only with respect to task and evidence inputs. I compiled the exact frozen tests/tools/score.py into a Python namespace using the supplied Python312 executable, retained its real POLICY path, substituted only _read_json with synthetic suite dictionaries and used an in-memory output Path to capture write_text results. No source or harness edits occurred. tests/tools/score.py:35-48 reads gate results first, requires every gate score > its 0.0 threshold, sets scored_ran=gates_passed and scored_data is not None, and sets all scored dimensions to zero unless scored_ran. It calculates only sum(weight*scored_dimension)/sum(weights), applies strict functional >0.05, and writes reward=0 unless gates AND floors pass. Lines 59-60 persist that reward; line 83 returns 1 for a gate failure, 0 otherwise. Executed inputs (render,constraints; functional,polish,visual) and observed outputs: (0,1;1,1,1) => return 1, reward 0, weighted_score 0, gates_passed 0, floors_passed 0; (1,0;1,1,1) => same. Both failing-gate cases recorded four skipped CTRF tests (floor and all three scored dimensions), despite supplying perfect scored inputs. Passing gates with no scored data => return 0, reward 0, floors_passed 0, four skipped CTRF tests. (1,1;0,1,1) => return 0, weighted_score 0.4, reward 0, floors_passed 0. (1,1;0.05,1,1) => weighted_score 0.43, reward 0, floors_passed 0. (1,1;0.050001,1,1) => weighted_score/reward 0.43, floors_passed 1, proving the strict boundary and four-decimal rounding. (1,1;1,1,1) => reward 1.0. (1,1;1,0,0) => reward 0.6. These are scorer fixtures, not measured judge assessments of apps. NaN render, boolean render, missing constraints, and missing functional were also rejected with ValueError; tests/tools/score.py:86-91 maps such exceptions to exit 2 in real CLI use.

Harness ordering: tests/test.sh:60-61 initializes zero reward and installs the cleanup trap. Lines 212-222 remove stale scored outputs, execute only the gates suite, run score.py, and exit immediately on scorer status 1; any other nonzero scorer status writes plain zero and exits. The scored invocation first appears at line 224, after this case statement. Lines 224-227 then execute the scored suite and recompute final reward, replacing errors with zero. A suite timeout/nonzero run exits before final positive scoring. The interim gates-only scorer output is zero, as the executed fixture confirms. Thus a failed gate cannot enter the scored invocation through the inspected control flow, and pre-existing scored output cannot rescue it. This shell branch was inspected, not run in a verifier container. SHA256/byte comparisons against the frozen canonical template were exact for tests/scoring.toml (95f70d6e06aae5e765b2309d88c444aa36d4cd82763ea2212781b6a99311bbba), tests/tools/score.py (13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e), and tests/test.sh (bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa).

Semantic dead-app defense and attempted witnesses: a polished static workspace whose Run never executes authored text is explicitly rejected by tests/gates/render/judge.toml:23-27, which requires a new marker in both preview and console through ordinary Run and says "A Run control that does nothing fails". A health-only server with localStorage saves cannot satisfy tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29: an actual UI write plus exact identity/title/filename/source retrieved twice in an independent clean context are required. The prompt supplies that context lifecycle at tests/gates/constraints/prompt.md:24-33; same-context tabs are explicitly insufficient. The synthetic perfect-style/failed-render and perfect-style/failed-constraints cases above prove that the corresponding gate verdicts cannot farm style reward. A hypothetical dimension report with functional=0 and perfect style is defeated by the floor. Even the three editor presentation criteria plus both theme criteria together weigh only 0.9/32.7=0.0275229358, below 0.05, before considering that theme preservation itself requires existing successful output. Because the functional weights are multiples of 0.05, crossing the floor needs at least 1.65/32.7=0.0504587156 observed weight. This threshold follows the mandated shared policy; it is not a license to substitute UI-only evidence for required successful controls.

Conforming alternatives considered: a native-looking workspace with an initially empty library, a server-rendered saved library rather than a JSON endpoint, different control labels/layouts, and no optional Auto-run control can still establish ordinary Run and server save/read. tests/gates/render/prompt.md:14-20 accepts an empty library and avoids feature-completeness additions; tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29 explicitly accepts the discovered response representation and server-rendered documents; tests/app_context.md:16 says missing Auto-run alone cannot fail Render/Constraints. These features avoid a false gate zero for equivalent implementations. The full-credit and function-only scorer fixtures above confirm no hidden gate mass or style floor. I did not build or browser-run these alternative apps and do not claim empirical judge acceptance for them.

Supporting raw runtime evidence and limits: independently inspected qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json, its S01.startup_ready, S21.saved_records_browser_reload and S17.manual_run_independent_of_autorun evidence, and corresponding workspace_flow.cjs/library_flow.cjs driver sections. Raw manual-off Run has marker count 0 -> 1 and body "auto-off"; reload evidence preserves two distinct records with exact fields; startup evidence has populated source, preview, and log without manual Run. Recomputed hashes match all recorded app files and driver files plus frozen functional judge/prompt hashes. These observations support a working golden implementation, but they are direct pinned Playwright product checks, not this complete gate suite and not a RewardKit/LLM judge run. RESULTS.json explicitly records paid_provider=false, browser_driver="direct pinned Playwright", oracle_score_claimed=false and wall_seconds=98.02680282300571. That duration is not judge timing. No full configured judge, hosted QC, Oracle score, or target-model score was measured in this review. The Pass is for this row's inspected gate ordering, zero mass, dead-app prerequisites and directly executed scorer calculations; full evaluator-runtime evidence remains separate, as required by current policy.
